title.zh: 卷270 列傳五十七 郝浴 杨素蕴 郭琇
title.en: Volume 270 Biographies 57: Hao Yu, Yang Suyun, Guo Xiu
title.raw: 卷270 列傳五十七 郝浴 杨素蕴 郭琇

sentences.zh: 列傳五十七

translations.literal: Biographies 57
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 57

sentences.zh: 郝浴子林楊素蘊郭琇

translations.literal: Hao Yu, his son Lin, Yang Suyun, Guo Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yu, his son Lin, Yang Suyun, and Guo Xiu

sentences.zh: 郝浴，字雪海，直隸定州人。

translations.literal: Hao Yu, style name Xuehai, was a native of Dingzhou in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Yu, whose style was Xuehai, came from Dingzhou in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 少有志操，負氣節。

translations.literal: In youth he had lofty resolve and bore himself with moral backbone.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed strong purpose and held fast to his principles.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi and was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 八年，改湖廣道御史，巡按四川。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to censor of the Huguang circuit and made an inspection tour of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was reassigned as censor of the Huguang circuit and sent on an inspection tour of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠將孫可望、李定國等降明，為桂王將，據川南為寇，師討之，郡縣吏率軍前除授，恣為貪虐。

translations.literal: At the time Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and other generals of Zhang Xianzhong had surrendered to the Ming and served as generals of the Prince of Gui, holding the south of Sichuan as bandits; as the army campaigned against them, prefectural and county officials appointed ahead of the troops indulged in greed and cruelty as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kewang, Li Dingguo, and other commanders once under Zhang Xianzhong had gone over to the Ming and now served the Prince of Gui, raiding from bases in southern Sichuan. As imperial forces moved against them, officials in the prefectures and counties were often appointed in advance of the army and abused their power with greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 浴至，嚴約束，廉民間疾苦，將吏始斂跡。

translations.literal: When Yu arrived he imposed strict discipline, investigated the people's hardships, and the officers and clerks at last restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu took up his post he enforced strict discipline, looked into the people's hardships, and the military and civil officers finally checked their excesses.

sentences.zh: 九年，平西王吳三桂與固山額真李國翰分兵復成都、嘉定、敘州、重慶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Prince of Pingxi, Wu Sangui, and the gushan ejen Li Guohan divided their forces to recover Chengdu, Jiading, Xuzhou, and Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Prince of Pingxi, Wu Sangui, and the banner general Li Guohan led separate columns to retake Chengdu, Jiading, Xuzhou, and Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 已而兩路兵俱敗，三桂退駐綿州。

translations.literal: Before long both columns were defeated, and Sangui withdrew to garrison at Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both columns were beaten, and Sangui fell back to hold Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 浴在保寧監臨鄉試，可望將數万人薄城，浴飛檄邀三桂，激以大義，謂「不死於賊，必死於法」。

translations.literal: Yu was at Baoning supervising the provincial examination when Kewang led tens of thousands to press the city; Yu sent an urgent dispatch inviting Sangui, rousing him with the call of duty, saying, "If you do not die at the hands of the rebels, you will die by the law."
translations.idiomatic: While Yu was at Baoning overseeing the provincial examinations, Kewang advanced with tens of thousands and pressed the city. Yu sent an urgent message summoning Sangui, appealing to duty: "If you do not die fighting the rebels, you will die under the law."

sentences.zh: 踰月，三桂乃赴援，可望等引去。

translations.literal: After more than a month Sangui at last came to the rescue, and Kewang and the others withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Sangui finally marched to relieve the siege, and Kewang and his forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 浴在圍城中，上詔詢收川方略，疏言：「秦兵苦轉餉，川兵苦待哺，故必秦不助川而後秦可保；

translations.literal: While Yu was in the besieged city the emperor issued an edict asking for strategy to recover Sichuan; he memorialized, saying: "Qin troops suffer from transporting provisions, and Sichuan troops suffer from waiting to be fed; therefore Qin must not aid Sichuan before Qin itself can be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: Still inside the besieged city, Yu received an imperial edict asking how Sichuan might be recovered. He memorialized: "The forces from Shaanxi are worn down hauling supplies, while the Sichuan troops are worn down waiting to be fed. Shaanxi must therefore stop subsidizing Sichuan before Shaanxi itself can be kept secure;

sentences.zh: 川不冀秦助而後川可圖。

translations.literal: Sichuan must not look to Qin for aid before Sichuan can be taken in hand.
translations.idiomatic: and Sichuan must stop counting on Shaanxi's help before Sichuan can truly be brought under control."

sentences.zh: 成都地大且要，灌口一水，襟帶三十州縣。

translations.literal: Chengdu is vast and strategically vital; the single waterway at Guankou binds together thirty prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu is broad, fertile, and strategically vital; the irrigation channel at Guankou alone ties together thirty prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 若移兵成都，照籍屯田，開耕一年，可當秦運三年。

translations.literal: If troops were shifted to Chengdu and garrison farming were organized by household registers, one year of cultivation could equal three years of Qin transport.
translations.idiomatic: If troops were stationed at Chengdu and organized for garrison farming by household register, one year's cultivation could replace three years of grain shipped from Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 所難者牛種，倘令土司出牛，撫臣與立券，豐年還其值，當無不聽命。

translations.literal: The difficulty lies in oxen and seed; if native chiefs were ordered to supply oxen and the provincial commissioner issued bonds, repaying their value in good harvest years, they would surely obey.
translations.idiomatic: The hard part is oxen and seed stock. If the native chiefs were asked to supply oxen and the provincial commissioner issued bonds to be repaid in good harvest years, they would surely comply.

sentences.zh: 嘉定據上游，饒茶、鹽，令暫易穀種，則牛、種俱不難辦也。

translations.literal: Jiading lies on the upper reaches, rich in tea and salt; if grain and seed were temporarily exchanged there, then both oxen and seed would not be hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Jiading sits upstream and is rich in tea and salt; if grain were temporarily traded there for seed, both oxen and seed could be obtained without great difficulty.

sentences.zh: 臣故謂開屯便。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore holds that opening garrison farms would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore urge that opening garrison farms is the better course.

sentences.zh: 川所患者滇寇也，滇寇所恃，不過皮兜、布鎧、鳥銃、濩刀，善於騰山踰嶺。

translations.literal: What Sichuan suffers from is the Yunnan bandits; what the Yunnan bandits rely on is no more than leather shields, cloth armor, muskets, and broadswords, and skill at scaling mountains and crossing ridges.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's affliction is the Yunnan raiders, who rely on little more than leather shields, cloth armor, muskets, and broadswords, and on their skill at climbing mountains and crossing ridges.

sentences.zh: 蜀中土官土兵，其技尤嫻於此。

translations.literal: The native chiefs and native troops of Shu are even more skilled in these arts.
translations.idiomatic: The native chiefs and native troops of Shu are even more practiced in such fighting.

sentences.zh: 若拔其精銳為前茅，以滿洲驍騎為後勁，疾雷迅霆，賊必鳥獸散。

translations.literal: If their elite were selected as vanguard and Manchu fierce cavalry as rear guard, moving like thunder and lightning, the bandits would surely scatter like birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: If their best fighters were taken as vanguard and Manchu cavalry as rear guard, striking like thunder, the rebels would scatter like startled birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 臣故謂用土兵便。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore holds that employing native troops would be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore urge that using native troops is the better course.

sentences.zh: 」上以其言可採，下部議。

translations.literal: " The emperor found his words acceptable and referred them to the ministries for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor found his advice worth adopting and referred it to the ministries for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 部議謂戰守事當聽三桂主之，遂報寢。

translations.literal: The ministries held that matters of campaigning and defense should be left to Sangui's decision, and the memorial was reported shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries ruled that campaigning and defense should be left to Sangui, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 浴又言：「土賊投誠，給劄授官，恣行劫掠為民害。

translations.literal: Yu also said: "Native bandits who surrender are given warrants and appointed to office, yet roam freely in plunder and harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yu also wrote: "When native bandits surrender they are given warrants and offices, yet they still raid at will and prey on the people.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後原歸伍者歸伍，原為民者，令有司造冊編丁，免牛租，除雜派，就熟地開徵，俾有定額。

translations.literal: I ask that hereafter those who were originally soldiers return to the ranks, and those who were originally civilians be entered in registers by the local authorities, exempted from ox rent, freed from miscellaneous levies, and assessed on cultivated land so that fixed quotas may be set.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter let those who were soldiers return to the ranks; for those who were civilians, let local officials register households, exempt ox rent, abolish miscellaneous levies, and levy taxes on cultivated land at fixed rates."

sentences.zh: 」疏議行。

translations.literal: " The memorial was deliberated and approved.
translations.idiomatic: " That memorial was approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 三桂入四川，浸驕橫，部下多不法，憚浴嚴正，輒禁止沿路塘報。

translations.literal: When Sangui entered Sichuan he grew increasingly arrogant; many of his subordinates acted unlawfully, and fearing Yu's severity they repeatedly blocked relay reports along the route.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangui entered Sichuan he grew ever more overbearing. Many of his men broke the law, and fearing Yu's strictness they repeatedly blocked courier reports along the roads.

sentences.zh: 浴上言：「臣忝司朝廷耳目，而壅閼若此，安用臣為？

translations.literal: Yu memorialized: "Your subject is charged to serve as the court's eyes and ears, yet if obstruction is such as this, of what use is your subject?
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized: "I am charged to serve as the court's eyes and ears. If communications are blocked like this, what use am I to the throne?

sentences.zh: 」及保寧圍解，頒賞將士，三桂以冠服與浴，浴不受。

translations.literal: " When the siege of Baoning was lifted rewards were distributed to officers and men; Sangui offered Yu robes and cap, but Yu refused them.
translations.idiomatic: " When the siege of Baoning was lifted and rewards were handed out, Sangui offered Yu ceremonial dress, but Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「平賊乃平西王責。

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Suppressing the bandits is the Prince of Pingxi's duty.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Crushing the rebels is the Prince of Pingxi's responsibility.

sentences.zh: 臣司風憲，不預軍事，而以臣預賞，非黨臣則忌臣也。

translations.literal: Your subject oversees discipline and does not take part in military affairs; to include your subject in the reward is either to court your subject or to begrudge your subject.
translations.idiomatic: I oversee discipline and had no part in the fighting. To include me in the reward is either to court me or to mark me for suspicion.

sentences.zh: 」因陳三桂擁兵觀望狀，三桂深銜之。

translations.literal: " He also described Sangui's holding troops and watching from the sidelines, and Sangui deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: " He also described how Sangui held his army back and waited on events, and Sangui came to hate him deeply.

sentences.zh: 浴劾永寧總兵柏永馥臨陣退縮，廣元副將胡一鵬驕悍不法，並命奪官逮治。

translations.literal: Yu impeached Yongning regional commander Bai Yongfu for shrinking back in battle and Guangyuan vice commander Hu Yipeng for arrogance and lawlessness, ordering both stripped of office and arrested for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Yu impeached Bai Yongfu, regional commander at Yongning, for flinching in battle, and Hu Yipeng, vice commander at Guangyuan, for arrogance and lawlessness, and had both stripped of rank and arrested.

sentences.zh: 降將董顯忠等以副將銜題授司道，恣睢虐民，浴复疏劾，改原職。

translations.literal: The surrendered generals Dong Xianzhong and others were nominated with vice-commander titles for provincial posts and tyrannized the people; Yu again memorialized against them and they were returned to their former ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered generals such as Dong Xianzhong had been nominated at vice-commander rank for provincial posts and abused the people. Yu impeached them again and they were reduced to their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 三桂嗾顯忠等入京陳辨，浴坐鐫秩去。

translations.literal: Sangui incited Xianzhong and the others to go to the capital to plead their case, and Yu was demoted and dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui prompted Xianzhong and the others to go to the capital to defend themselves, and Yu was demoted and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大學士馮銓、成克鞏、呂宮等交章薦浴，三桂乃摭浴保寧奏捷疏有「親冒矢石」語，指為冒功，論劾，部議當坐死，上命寬之，流徙奉天。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, Lü Gong, and others submitted successive memorials recommending Yu; Sangui then seized upon Yu's victory memorial from Baoning, which contained the phrase "personally braved arrows and stones," and charged him with claiming merit falsely; after impeachment the ministries held he should suffer death, but the emperor ordered leniency and he was exiled to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, Lü Gong, and others repeatedly recommended Yu. Sangui then seized on Yu's Baoning victory memorial, which said he had "personally braved arrows and stones," and accused him of false claims to merit. After impeachment the ministries ruled he deserved death, but the emperor commuted the sentence and exiled him to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 大學士馮銓、成克鞏、呂宮皆以薦浴罣吏議。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, and Lü Gong were all implicated in official censure for recommending Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Cheng Kegong, and Lü Gong were all censured for having recommended Yu.

sentences.zh: 浴至戍所，益潛心義理之學，嗜孟子及二程遺書，以「致知格物」顏其廬，刻苦厲志。

translations.literal: When Yu reached his place of exile he devoted himself ever more to the study of moral principle, cherished Mencius and the surviving works of the Cheng brothers, and inscribed his dwelling with "extending knowledge and investigating things," striving bitterly to steel his will.
translations.idiomatic: At his place of exile Yu threw himself into moral philosophy, devouring Mencius and the Cheng brothers' writings. He labeled his hut "Extending Knowledge and Investigating Things" and disciplined himself with stern resolve.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，聖祖幸奉天，浴迎謁道左，具陳始末，上為動容，慰勞良久。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor visited Fengtian; Yu met him by the roadside and set forth the whole story; the emperor was moved and comforted him at length.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Kangxi the emperor visited Fengtian. Yu met him by the road, told the whole story of his case, and moved the emperor, who spoke with him at length in consolation.

sentences.zh: 十二年，三桂反，尚書王熙、給事中劉沛先薦浴，為部議所格。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Sangui rebelled; Minister Wang Xi and supervising secretary Liu Peixian recommended Yu first, but the recommendation was blocked in ministry deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when Sangui rebelled, Minister Wang Xi and supervising secretary Liu Peixian were the first to recommend Yu, but the ministries blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 十四年，侍郎魏象樞复疏言：「浴血性過人，才守學識，臣皆愧不及。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Vice Minister Wei Xiangshu again memorialized, saying: "Yu surpasses others in native courage; in talent, integrity, and learning your subject is ashamed to fall short.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Vice Minister Wei Xiangshu memorialized again: "Yu's courage is beyond the ordinary. In talent, integrity, and learning I am ashamed to compare with him.

sentences.zh: 使在西蜀操尺寸之權，豈肯如羅森輩俯首從逆？

translations.literal: Had he held even a small measure of authority in western Shu, how could he have bowed his head and followed rebellion like Luo Sen and his kind?
translations.idiomatic: Had he held even a small measure of authority in western Shu, would he have bowed to rebellion like Luo Sen and his kind?

sentences.zh: 臣子立朝，各有本末。

translations.literal: Ministers who serve at court each have their own beginning and end.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister who serves at court has his own story from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 當日參浴者三桂也，使三桂始終恭順，方且任以腹心。

translations.literal: The one who impeached Yu then was Sangui; had Sangui remained always dutiful, the court would even have entrusted him with its innermost confidence.
translations.idiomatic: The man who impeached Yu then was Sangui. Had Sangui remained loyal, the court would even have trusted him with its innermost affairs.

sentences.zh: 浴一書生耳，即老死徙所，誰復問之？

translations.literal: Yu is only a scholar; even if he died of old age in exile, who would ask after him?
translations.idiomatic: Yu is only a scholar. Even if he died in exile, who would have noticed?

sentences.zh: 今三桂叛矣，天下無不恨三桂，即無不憐浴。

translations.literal: Now Sangui has rebelled; under Heaven none do not hate Sangui, and none do not pity Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Now Sangui has rebelled. All under Heaven hates Sangui—and pities Yu.

sentences.zh: 浴當三桂身居王爵，手握兵柄，不畏威，不附勢，致為所仇。

translations.literal: When Yu faced Sangui, who held princely rank and grasped military power, he did not fear authority and did not cling to power, and thus became Sangui's enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui held princely rank and military power, Yu neither feared his might nor courted his favor, and so became his enemy.

sentences.zh: 三桂之所仇，正國家之所取，何忍棄之？

translations.literal: Whom Sangui hates is precisely whom the state should take up—how can we bear to cast Yu aside?
translations.idiomatic: Whom Sangui hated is precisely whom the state should value. How can we abandon him?

sentences.zh: 」上乃召浴還，复授湖廣道御史。

translations.literal: " The emperor then summoned Yu back and again appointed him censor of the Huguang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor recalled Yu and reappointed him censor of the Huguang circuit.

sentences.zh: 時陝西提督王輔臣叛應三桂，浴疏言：「大兵進剿平涼，宜於西安、潼關用重兵屯駐，以待策應。

translations.literal: At the time Shaanxi provincial commander Wang Fuchen rebelled in support of Sangui; Yu memorialized, saying: "As the main army advances to suppress Pingliang, heavy forces should be stationed at Xi'an and Tongguan to await coordinated action.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi provincial commander Wang Fuchen rebelled in support of Sangui, Yu wrote: "As the main army advances against Pingliang, heavy forces should be stationed at Xi'an and Tongguan to support the campaign.

sentences.zh: 用鄖陽之兵攻興安，調河南之兵入武關，直取漢中，逆賊計日可擒。

translations.literal: Use the troops of Xiangyang to attack Xing'an, move Henan troops through Wuguan, and strike straight for Hanzhong; the rebels can be taken within days.
translations.idiomatic: Send the Xiangyang troops against Xing'an, move Henan troops through Wuguan, and strike straight for Hanzhong—the rebels can be taken within days."

sentences.zh: 」上然之，下其疏諸帥。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved and circulated his memorial to the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and sent the memorial to the field commanders.

sentences.zh: 復請禁苛徵，恤民困，止督、撫、提、鎮坐​​名題補之例。

translations.literal: He again asked to forbid harsh levies, relieve the people's distress, and stop the practice by which governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders merely signed names for nominations and appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged an end to harsh levies, relief for the people's hardships, and an end to the practice whereby governors, provincial commanders, and regional commanders merely signed their names on nominations.

sentences.zh: 章十數上，皆中時弊。

translations.literal: He submitted more than a dozen memorials, all striking at the abuses of the day.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than a dozen memorials, each hitting a current abuse squarely.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命巡視兩淮鹽政，嚴剔宿蠹，增課六十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to inspect the salt administration of the two Huai circuits, rigorously rooting out long-standing corruption and increasing revenue by more than six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to inspect the Liang-Huai salt administration, root out entrenched corruption, and increase revenue by more than six hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚大饑，發倉米賑救，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: When Huai and Yang suffered great famine he released granary grain for relief and saved a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Huai and Yang regions he opened the granaries and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢左僉都御史，遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and then transferred to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and then to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 廣西新經喪亂，民生凋瘵，浴專意撫綏，疏陳調劑四策，請裁兵、汰馬、防要害、簡精銳；

translations.literal: Guangxi had newly passed through turmoil and the people's livelihood was wasted; Yu devoted himself to pacification and memorialized four measures of adjustment, asking to cut troops, cull horses, guard key points, and select elite forces;
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi had only lately emerged from rebellion and the people were destitute. Yu devoted himself to pacification and proposed four measures of adjustment: cut troops, cull horses, guard key points, and keep only elite units;

sentences.zh: 復請停鼓鑄，改米徵銀，复南寧、太平、思恩諸府縣行鹽舊制：上輒報可。

translations.literal: he also asked to halt minting, convert grain levies to silver, and restore the old salt regulations in Nanning, Taiping, Si'en, and other prefectures and counties—the emperor invariably approved.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to halt minting, convert grain taxes to silver payments, and restore the old salt regulations in Nanning, Taiping, Si'en, and other districts. The emperor approved each request.

sentences.zh: 時南疆底定，滿洲兵撤還京師。

translations.literal: At the time the southern frontier had been settled and Manchu troops were withdrawn to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: By then the southern frontier had been pacified and Manchu troops were withdrawn to the capital.

sentences.zh: 浴疏言撫標兵不宜裁減，下部議，留其半。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized that the governor's banner troops should not be reduced; after ministry deliberation half were retained.
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued that the governor's banner troops should not be cut. After deliberation the ministries kept half their strength.

sentences.zh: 又請為死事巡撫馬雄鎮、傅弘烈建祠桂林，知府劉浩、知縣周岱生為孫延齡所戕，疏請予卹。

translations.literal: He also asked that shrines be built at Guilin for the governors who died in service, Ma Xiongzhen and Fu Honglie, and that relief be granted to prefect Liu Hao and magistrate Zhou Daisheng, who were killed by Sun Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for shrines at Guilin to the fallen governors Ma Xiongzhen and Fu Honglie, and posthumous honors for Prefect Liu Hao and Magistrate Zhou Daisheng, who had been killed by Sun Yanling.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，士民泣送者數千里不絕。

translations.literal: When his coffin returned, officials and commoners who wept and escorted him stretched unbroken for thousands of li.
translations.idiomatic: As his coffin was borne home, mourners among officials and commoners lined the road for thousands of li without a break.

sentences.zh: 初，傅弘烈以軍事急，移庫金七萬有奇、米七千餘石供餉，浴請以庫項扣抵。

translations.literal: Earlier, because military affairs were urgent, Fu Honglie had drawn more than seventy thousand taels from the treasury and more than seven thousand shi of grain for provisions; Yu asked that treasury accounts be offset against these sums.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when military needs were urgent, Fu Honglie had drawn more than seventy thousand taels from the treasury and more than seven thousand shi of grain for supplies. Yu asked that these sums be charged against the treasury accounts.

sentences.zh: 及卒，布政使崔維雅署巡撫，劾浴侵欺，命郎中蘇赫、陳光祖往按，如維雅言。

translations.literal: After Yu died, Provincial Administration Commissioner Cui Weiya acted as governor and impeached Yu for embezzlement and fraud; the emperor ordered Directors Su He and Chen Guangzu to investigate on site, and they found as Cui had alleged.
translations.idiomatic: After Yu's death, Provincial Administration Commissioner Cui Weiya, acting as governor, impeached him for embezzlement. The emperor sent Directors Su He and Chen Guangzu to investigate, and they confirmed Cui's charges.

sentences.zh: 部議奪官追償。

translations.literal: The ministries held that his office should be posthumously revoked and restitution pursued.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries ruled that his rank should be posthumously revoked and restitution demanded.

sentences.zh: 上知浴廉，諭所動錢糧非入己，從寬免追。

translations.literal: The emperor knew Yu was incorrupt and declared that the funds and grain he had moved had not entered his own pocket; leniency was granted and recovery was waived.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Yu's integrity, the emperor ruled that the funds and grain had not gone into his own pocket and waived restitution.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，子林訟父冤，復原官，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year his son Lin sued to clear his father's name; Yu's former rank was restored and sacrificial honors and burial grants were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year his son Lin petitioned to clear his father's name. Yu's rank was restored and he was granted state sacrifices and burial honors.

sentences.zh: 林，字中美。

translations.literal: Lin, style name Zhongmei.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, whose style was Zhongmei,

sentences.zh: 康熙二十一年進士，授中書科中書，歷吏部郎中，亦以廉正稱。

translations.literal: passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-first year of Kangxi, was appointed a secretary in the Secretariat, served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel, and was likewise known for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: became a jinshi in the twenty-first year of Kangxi, served as a Secretariat secretary and later as a director in the Ministry of Personnel, and was likewise known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮部侍郎，加尚書銜。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of Rites and given the nominal rank of Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Vice Minister of Rites with ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 致仕，卒。

translations.literal: He retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and later died.

sentences.zh: 楊素蘊，字筠湄，陝西宜君人。

translations.literal: Yang Suyun, style name Junmei, was a native of Yijun in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Suyun, whose style was Junmei, came from Yijun in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，授直隸東明知縣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Dongming in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Shunzhi and was appointed magistrate of Dongming in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 東明當河決後，官舍城垣悉敗，民居殆盡，遺民依丘阜，僅數十家。

translations.literal: Dongming lay in the aftermath of a river breach; government buildings and city walls were all ruined, dwellings nearly all gone, and survivors clung to hillocks—only a few dozen households.
translations.idiomatic: Dongming had been devastated by a river breach. Government buildings and city walls lay in ruins, homes were nearly gone, and survivors clustered on hillocks—only a few dozen households remained.

sentences.zh: 素蘊至，為繕城郭，招集流亡，三年戶增至萬餘。

translations.literal: When Suyun arrived he repaired the walls and city, gathered the displaced, and within three years households increased to more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Suyun arrived he rebuilt the walls and city, gathered the displaced, and within three years households rose to more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 山東群盜任鳳亭等剽掠旁郡，擾及畿南。

translations.literal: Bandits in Shandong such as Ren Fengting plundered neighboring prefectures and disturbed the capital region's south.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong bandits such as Ren Fengting raided neighboring prefectures and even threatened the southern approaches to the capital.

sentences.zh: 素蘊設計降其渠，散其脅從。

translations.literal: Suyun devised a plan to induce their leaders to surrender and disperse their followers.
translations.idiomatic: Suyun devised a plan to induce the ringleaders to surrender and disperse their followers.

sentences.zh: 十七年，舉卓異，行取，授四川道御史。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was rated outstanding, selected for capital service, and appointed censor of the Sichuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was rated outstanding, selected for capital service, and appointed censor of the Sichuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「臣言官也，宜以言為事。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Your subject is a speaking official and ought to make speech his business.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "I am a remonstrating official and ought to make speaking out my duty.

sentences.zh: 然今天下所患，正在議論多而成功少。

translations.literal: Yet what the realm suffers from today is precisely that discussion is abundant while achievement is scarce.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what afflicts the realm today is talk in abundance and results in short supply.

sentences.zh: 國家建官分職，各有所事。

translations.literal: The state establishes offices and divides duties, each with its own charge.
translations.idiomatic: The state establishes offices and divides duties, each with its proper charge.

sentences.zh: 誠使司舉劾，籌財用，任封疆，理刑獄，各舉其職，則平天下無餘事。

translations.literal: If truly those who oversee impeachment, plan revenue, hold frontier posts, and administer punishments each performed their duties, then pacifying the realm would leave nothing undone.
translations.idiomatic: If those who oversee impeachment, plan revenue, hold frontier posts, and administer justice each did their proper work, pacifying the realm would require nothing more.

sentences.zh: 更原皇上推誠御物，肅大閒，寬小眚，俾人人得展其才，尤端本澄源之要也。

translations.literal: I further pray that Your Majesty treat all things with sincere openness, be stern in great matters and lenient in small faults, and let every man display his talent—this above all is the way to rectify the root and clarify the source.
translations.idiomatic: I further pray that Your Majesty treat all with sincere openness, be stern in great matters and lenient in small faults, and let every man display his talent. That above all is how to rectify the root and clarify the source."

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂鎮雲南，郡縣吏得自闢署，謂之「西選」。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Sangui governed Yunnan; prefectural and county officials could be appointed on his own authority, called the "western selection."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Sangui governed Yunnan. Prefectural and county officials could be appointed at his own discretion—the so-called "western selection."

sentences.zh: 漸乃題用朝臣，無復顧忌。

translations.literal: Gradually he began nominating court officials as well, without further restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually he began nominating court officials as well, without further restraint.

sentences.zh: 素蘊疏言：「三桂以上湖南道胡允等十員題補雲南各道，並有奉差部員在內，深足駭異。

translations.literal: Suyun memorialized, saying: "Sangui has nominated ten men including Hu Yun of the Hunan circuit to fill the various Yunnan posts, and among them are ministry officials on imperial assignment—this is deeply shocking.
translations.idiomatic: Suyun wrote: "Sangui has nominated ten men, including Hu Yun of the Hunan circuit, to fill Yunnan's circuit posts, and among them are ministry officials on imperial assignment. This is deeply alarming.

sentences.zh: 爵祿者人主之大柄，綱紀者朝廷之大防，柄不可移，防不可潰。

translations.literal: Rank and stipend are the sovereign's great handle; discipline is the court's great bulwark—the handle must not be shifted, the bulwark must not be breached.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and stipend are the sovereign's great prerogative; discipline is the court's great bulwark. The prerogative must not be shifted, the bulwark must not be breached.

sentences.zh: 前此經略用人，特命二部不得掣肘，亦惟以軍前效用及所轄五省各官酌量題請，從未聞敢以他行省及現任京官坐缺定銜者也。

translations.literal: When the frontier commissioner appointed men before, the two ministries were specially ordered not to obstruct him, yet nominations were weighed only for merit before the army and for officials within the five provinces under his charge; never was it heard that he dared fix ranks for vacancies in other provinces or for serving capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier commissioner appointed men before, the two ministries were ordered not to obstruct him, yet nominations were weighed only for merit in the field and for officials within his five provinces. Never was it heard that he dared fix ranks for vacancies in other provinces or for serving capital officials.

sentences.zh: 且疏稱求於滇省既苦索駿無從，求於遠方又恐叱馭不速，則湖南、四川距雲南猶近，若京師、山東、江南相去萬里，不知其所謂遠者更在何方？

translations.literal: Moreover his memorial says that seeking within Yunnan he has found no suitable men, and seeking afar he fears they will not arrive in time—yet Hunan and Sichuan are still near Yunnan; if the capital, Shandong, and Jiangnan lie ten thousand li away, where can his "afar" be?
translations.idiomatic: His memorial says that within Yunnan he can find no suitable men, and that men from afar may not arrive in time. Yet Hunan and Sichuan are still near Yunnan. If the capital, Shandong, and Jiangnan lie ten thousand li away, where exactly is his "afar"?

sentences.zh: 皇上特假便宜，不過許其就近調補。

translations.literal: The special discretion granted by Your Majesty amounts to no more than allowing local transfers nearby.
translations.idiomatic: The special discretion Your Majesty granted amounts to no more than allowing nearby transfers.

sentences.zh: 若盡天下之官，不分內外，不論遠近，皆可擇而取之，何如歸吏部銓授，尤為名正言順。

translations.literal: If all offices under Heaven, without distinction of inner or outer, near or far, may be chosen and taken, how much better to return appointment to the Ministry of Personnel by regular selection—that would be all the more proper in name and right.
translations.idiomatic: If every office under Heaven, without regard to inner or outer, near or far, may be chosen at will, how much better to return appointments to the Ministry of Personnel—that would be proper in name and right.

sentences.zh: 縱或云、貴新經開闢，料理乏人，諸臣才品為籓臣所素知，亦宜請旨令吏部簽補；

translations.literal: Even if Yunnan and Guizhou have been newly opened and lack men to manage affairs, and the talents of these officials are well known to the frontier lord, it is still fitting to request an edict and let the Ministry of Personnel sign and fill the posts;
translations.idiomatic: Even if Yunnan and Guizhou have only lately been opened and lack administrators, and the frontier lord knows these men's talents well, he should still request an edict and let the Ministry of Personnel sign and fill the posts;

sentences.zh: 乃徑行擬用，不亦輕名器而褻國體乎？

translations.literal: to proceed directly with proposed appointments—is this not to slight the vessels of honor and profane the state's dignity?
translations.idiomatic: to proceed directly with appointments—is this not to slight the vessels of honor and profane the dignity of the state?

sentences.zh: 人臣忠邪之分，起於一念之敬肆。

translations.literal: The division between loyal and treacherous ministers begins in a single thought of reverence or license.
translations.idiomatic: The line between loyal and treacherous ministers begins in a single thought of reverence or license.

sentences.zh: 籓臣易攵歷有年，應知大體。

translations.literal: The frontier lord has held power for many years and ought to understand the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier lord has held power for many years and ought to understand what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 此舉為封疆計，未必別有深心，然防微杜漸，當慎於幾先。

translations.literal: This act may be for the frontier's sake and not necessarily harbor another deep intent, yet to guard against trouble before it spreads one must be cautious at the first sign.
translations.idiomatic: This move may serve the frontier and need not spring from hidden designs, yet to check trouble before it spreads one must be cautious at the first sign.

sentences.zh: 祈申飭籓臣，嗣後惟力圖進取，加意撫綏，一切威福大權，俱宜禀自朝廷，則君恩臣誼兩盡其善。

translations.literal: I pray that the frontier lord be sternly admonished: hereafter let him strive only for advance and give added care to pacification; all great powers of authority and favor should be reported to the court—then sovereign grace and ministerial duty will both reach their best.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that the frontier lord be sternly warned: hereafter let him strive for progress and give added care to pacification. All great powers of authority and favor should come from the court—then sovereign grace and ministerial duty will both be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 」疏下部。

translations.literal: " The memorial was referred to the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was sent to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 十八年，聖祖即位，輔臣柄政，出素蘊為川北道。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Sacred Ancestor ascended the throne; the assisting ministers held power and transferred Suyun out to the North Sichuan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, when the Sacred Ancestor ascended the throne, the assisting ministers held power and transferred Suyun to the North Sichuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 三桂見素蘊前奏，惡之，具疏辨，並摘「防微杜漸」語，謂意含隱射，語伏危機。

translations.literal: Sangui, seeing Suyun's earlier memorial, hated him and submitted a full memorial in rebuttal, seizing on the phrase "guard against trouble before it spreads" and claiming the meaning carried hidden insinuation and concealed a crisis in the wording.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui, seeing Suyun's earlier memorial, hated him and submitted a full rebuttal, seizing on the phrase "guard against trouble before it spreads" and claiming it carried hidden insinuation and concealed a threat.

sentences.zh: 詔責素蘊回奏，素蘊言：「防微杜漸，古今通義。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked Suyun and ordered him to reply; Suyun said: "Guarding against trouble before it spreads is a universal principle of past and present.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked Suyun and ordered a reply. Suyun said: "Guarding against trouble before it spreads is a universal principle of past and present.

sentences.zh: 臣但期籓臣每事盡善，為聖世純臣，非有他也。

translations.literal: Your subject only hopes the frontier lord will make every matter as good as possible and be a pure minister of this sage age—there is no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: I only hope the frontier lord will do every matter as well as possible and be a loyal minister of this sage age. I had no other intent.

sentences.zh: 」下部議，坐素蘊巧飾，當降調，罷歸。

translations.literal: " After ministry deliberation Suyun was found guilty of artful excuse, should be demoted, and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: " After deliberation the ministries found Suyun guilty of artful excuse, ruled he should be demoted, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 居十年，三桂反。

translations.literal: After ten years in retirement Sangui rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later Sangui rebelled.

sentences.zh: 尚書郝惟訥、冀如錫，侍郎楊永寧交章請起用，惟訥詞尤切，略言：「素蘊首劾三桂，雲當防微杜漸。

translations.literal: Ministers Hao Weina and Ji Ruxi and Vice Minister Yang Yongning submitted successive memorials asking that he be reemployed; Weina's words were especially urgent, saying in summary: "Suyun was the first to impeach Sangui, declaring that one must guard against trouble before it spreads.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Hao Weina and Ji Ruxi and Vice Minister Yang Yongning repeatedly asked that he be reemployed. Weina was especially urgent, writing in summary: "Suyun was the first to impeach Sangui, warning that trouble must be checked before it spreads.

sentences.zh: 在當日反狀未形，似屬杞憂。

translations.literal: At the time the signs of rebellion had not yet appeared, and it seemed idle worry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time rebellion had not yet appeared, and it seemed idle worry.

sentences.zh: 由今觀之，則素蘊先見甚明，且為國直陳，奮不自顧，其剛腸正氣，實有大過人者！

translations.literal: Viewed from today, Suyun's foresight is very clear; moreover he spoke straight for the state and strove without regard for himself—his firm integrity and upright spirit truly surpass others!
translations.idiomatic: Seen from today, Suyun's foresight is unmistakable. He spoke straight for the state and strove without regard for himself. His firm integrity and upright spirit truly surpass ordinary men!

sentences.zh: 亟宜優錄。

translations.literal: He should urgently be favored with appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He should urgently be honored with appointment.

sentences.zh: 」乃命發湖廣軍前，以原品用。

translations.literal: " He was then ordered sent to the Huguang front at his former rank.
translations.idiomatic: " He was ordered to the Huguang front at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 會丁父憂，服闋，乃赴軍前。

translations.literal: He happened to enter mourning for his father; when the mourning period ended he went to the front.
translations.idiomatic: He was in mourning for his father; when the mourning ended he went to the front.

sentences.zh: 總督蔡毓榮題補湖廣提學道，部議當以現辦軍務參議道題補。

translations.literal: Governor-General Cai Yurong nominated him to fill the Huguang educational circuit, but the ministries held he should be nominated to the military affairs participation circuit then in active service.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Cai Yurong nominated him for the Huguang educational circuit, but the ministries ruled he should fill the military affairs participation circuit then in active service.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，題補下荊南道。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi he was nominated to fill the Lower Jingnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi he was appointed to the Lower Jingnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 時襄陽總兵楊來嘉、副將洪福等叛應三桂。

translations.literal: At the time Xiangyang regional commander Yang Laijia, vice commander Hong Fu, and others rebelled in support of Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiangyang regional commander Yang Laijia, Vice Commander Hong Fu, and others rebelled in support of Sangui.

sentences.zh: 大軍運餉，自襄至房、保路險C7，舟車不通，歲調襄陽、安陸、德安三郡丁夫擔負，餉苦不繼。

translations.literal: The main army transported provisions; from Xiangyang to Fang and Bao the road was rugged and neither boat nor cart could pass, and each year corvée laborers from the three prefectures of Xiangyang, Anlu, and De'an were levied to carry loads on their backs, so that provisions sorely failed to keep up.
translations.idiomatic: The main army moved supplies from Xiangyang toward Fang and Bao over rugged terrain where neither boats nor carts could pass. Each year corvée laborers from Xiangyang, Anlu, and De'an were levied to carry loads on their backs, and supplies constantly fell short.

sentences.zh: 素蘊訪知穀城有小溪可通舟，乃按行山谷開餉道，由是水運通利，省丁夫什九，軍乃無乏。

translations.literal: Suyun learned through inquiry that Gucheng had a small stream navigable by boat; he then surveyed the mountain valleys and opened a supply route, whereby water transport became efficient, corvée labor was reduced by nine-tenths, and the army was no longer short.
translations.idiomatic: Suyun learned that a small stream at Gucheng could carry boats. He surveyed the mountain valleys and opened a supply route, so water transport became efficient, corvée labor fell by nine-tenths, and the army was no longer short of supplies.

sentences.zh: 遷山西提學道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Shanxi educational circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Shanxi educational circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，任滿，薦舉擢通政司參議，累遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, when his term ended, he was raised by recommendation to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission and was promoted in succession to Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when his term ended, he was promoted by recommendation to Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission and later became Intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，上疏請賑。

translations.literal: Famine struck that year, and he memorialized asking for relief.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck that year he memorialized asking for relief.

sentences.zh: 甫拜疏，即檄州縣開倉賑給，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: As soon as his memorial was submitted he ordered the prefectures and counties to open granaries for relief, saving a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as his memorial went up he ordered the prefectures and counties to open the granaries, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 尋調湖廣巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 夏逢龍亂初定，脅從尚眾，人情恇擾，一夕數驚。

translations.literal: The rebellion of Xia Fenglong had just been settled; those coerced to follow were still numerous, hearts were fearful and unsettled, and in a single night alarms arose several times.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellion of Xia Fenglong had only just been suppressed. Many who had been coerced still remained, hearts were fearful and unsettled, and in a single night alarms arose several times.

sentences.zh: 素蘊首嚴告訐之禁，反側以安。

translations.literal: Suyun was the first to enforce strictly the ban on informers, and the wavering were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Suyun was the first to enforce strictly the ban on informers, and the wavering were pacified.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，大旱，疏請蠲免武昌等屬三十二州縣錢糧，上遣戶部郎中舒淑等會督撫勘災。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year a great drought struck; he memorialized asking exemption of taxes and grain for thirty-two prefectures and counties under Wuchang and elsewhere; the emperor sent Ministry of Revenue Director Shu Shu and others to join the governor-general and governor in surveying the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year a great drought struck. He memorialized to exempt taxes and grain for thirty-two prefectures and counties under Wuchang and elsewhere. The emperor sent Ministry of Revenue Director Shu Shu and others to join the governor-general and governor in surveying the disaster.

sentences.zh: 舒淑至武昌，素蘊適患暑疾，令布政使於養志從總督丁思孔往勘。

translations.literal: When Shu Shu reached Wuchang, Suyun happened to be ill with summer heat; he ordered Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yangzhi to accompany Governor-General Ding Sikong in the survey.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu Shu reached Wuchang, Suyun was ill with summer heat and ordered Provincial Administration Commissioner Yu Yangzhi to accompany Governor-General Ding Sikong on the survey.

sentences.zh: 尋稱病乞休，上疑其託疾，奪官。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and asked to retire; the emperor suspected he was feigning sickness and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pleaded illness and asked to retire. The emperor suspected he was feigning sickness and stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 命甫下而素蘊已卒。

translations.literal: The order had scarcely been issued when Suyun had already died.
translations.idiomatic: The order had scarcely been issued when Suyun died.

sentences.zh: 先是，湖北郡縣疾苦最甚者，如沔陽、江陵、漢陽、嘉魚濱江地陷未蠲賦額，咸寧、黃陂、景陵谷折，江夏、崇陽、武昌、通城、漢陽、漢川、雲夢、孝感、應城穀田科重，監利一年兩賦，為民害數十年。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the gravest hardships in Huguang's prefectures and counties: in Mianyang, Jiangling, Hanyang, and Jiayu, riverside land had sunk without exemption of tax quotas; in Xianning, Huangpi, and Jingling, grain yields were reduced by half; in Jiangxia, Chongyang, Wuchang, Tongcheng, Hanyang, Hanchuan, Yunmeng, Xiaogan, and Yingcheng, grain-field assessments were heavy; in Jianli there were two levies in one year—harms to the people for decades.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, among the gravest abuses in Huguang: in Mianyang, Jiangling, Hanyang, and Jiayu, sunken riverside land still bore full taxes; in Xianning, Huangpi, and Jingling, grain yields were assessed at half the true harvest; in Jiangxia, Chongyang, Wuchang, Tongcheng, Hanyang, Hanchuan, Yunmeng, Xiaogan, and Yingcheng, grain-field taxes were crushing; in Jianli two levies were collected in a single year—burdens that had harmed the people for decades.

sentences.zh: 素蘊得其實，條為兩疏。

translations.literal: Suyun obtained the facts and set them forth in two memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Suyun verified the facts and set them forth in two memorials.

sentences.zh: 未及上而病革，口授入遺疏，曰：「此疏行，吾目瞑矣！

translations.literal: Before he could submit them his illness turned critical; he dictated them into a deathbed memorial, saying: "When this memorial is carried out, my eyes may close!
translations.idiomatic: Before he could submit them his illness turned critical. He dictated a deathbed memorial, saying: "When this memorial is carried out, I can close my eyes!

sentences.zh: 郭琇，字華野，山東即墨人。

translations.literal: Guo Xiu, style name Huaye, was a native of Jimo in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu, whose style was Huaye, came from Jimo in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授江南吳江知縣。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed magistrate of Wujiang in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was appointed magistrate of Wujiang in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 材力強幹，善斷疑獄。

translations.literal: His talent and energy were strong and capable, and he was skilled at deciding doubtful cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was capable and forceful, and skilled at deciding difficult cases.

sentences.zh: 徵賦行版串法，胥吏不能為奸。

translations.literal: In collecting taxes he used the linked-register method, so clerks could not practice fraud.
translations.idiomatic: He collected taxes by the linked-register method, so clerks could not practice fraud.

sentences.zh: 居官七年，治行為江南最。

translations.literal: After seven years in office his administrative record was the finest in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in office his record was the finest in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，巡撫湯斌薦琇居心恬淡，蒞事精銳，請遷擢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Governor Tang Bin recommended Xiu as calm in mind, sharp in handling affairs, and asked that he be promoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Governor Tang Bin recommended Xiu as calm in mind and sharp in affairs, and asked that he be promoted.

sentences.zh: 部議以琇徵賦未如額，寢其奏，聖祖特許之，行取，授江南道御史。

translations.literal: The ministries held that Xiu's tax collection had not met quota and shelved the memorial, but the Sacred Ancestor specially approved it; he was selected for capital service and appointed censor of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries held that Xiu's tax collection had not met quota and shelved the memorial, but the Sacred Ancestor overruled them, selected him for capital service, and appointed him censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 時河督靳輔請停濬下河，築高家堰重堤，清丈堤外田畝以為屯田，謂可增歲收百餘萬。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Canal Director Jin Fu asked to halt dredging of the lower river, build heavy dikes at the Gaojia Weir, and survey fields outside the dikes for garrison farms, claiming annual revenue could be increased by more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Canal Director Jin Fu asked to halt dredging of the lower river, build heavy dikes at the Gaojia Weir, and survey fields outside the dikes for garrison farms, claiming annual revenue could rise by more than a million taels.

sentences.zh: 巡撫於成龍議不​​合，上令尚書佛倫往勘，主輔議。

translations.literal: Governor Yu Chenglong disagreed; the emperor ordered Minister Folun to investigate on site and upheld Fu's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yu Chenglong disagreed. The emperor ordered Minister Folun to investigate and upheld Fu's plan.

sentences.zh: 下九卿覈奏，尚書張玉書、左都御史徐乾學力言屯田擾民。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Nine Ministers for review; Minister Zhang Yushu and Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Qianxue strongly declared that garrison farms would disturb the people.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went to the Nine Ministers for review. Minister Zhang Yushu and Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Qianxue strongly argued that garrison farms would harm the people.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，琇疏劾輔治河無功，偏聽幕客陳潢阻濬下河。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Xiu memorialized impeaching Fu for achieving nothing in river control and listening only to his secretary Chen Huang, who blocked dredging of the lower river.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Xiu impeached Fu for achieving nothing in river control and for listening only to his secretary Chen Huang, who blocked dredging of the lower river.

sentences.zh: 上御乾清門，召諸大臣，下琇疏，令會同察議。

translations.literal: The emperor held court at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, summoned the ministers, circulated Xiu's memorial, and ordered joint investigation and deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held court at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, summoned the ministers, circulated Xiu's memorial, and ordered a joint investigation.

sentences.zh: 尋輔入覲，復召諸大臣與議。

translations.literal: Soon Fu came to audience at court, and the ministers were again summoned to deliberate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fu came to court for audience, and the ministers were summoned again to deliberate with him.

sentences.zh: 琇申言屯田害民，輔坐罷，而擢琇僉都御史。

translations.literal: Xiu again declared that garrison farms harmed the people; Fu was dismissed on that account, and Xiu was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu again argued that garrison farms harmed the people. Fu was dismissed, and Xiu was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大學士明珠柄政，與餘國柱比，頗營賄賂，權傾一時，久之為上所覺。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Mingzhu held power, paired with Yu Guozhu, and engaged extensively in bribes; his authority dominated the age, until long afterward the emperor perceived it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Mingzhu held power alongside Yu Guozhu and engaged extensively in bribery. His authority dominated the age until the emperor finally perceived it.

sentences.zh: 琇疏劾明珠與國柱結黨行私，詳列諸罪狀，並及佛倫、傅拉塔與輔等交通狀，於是明珠等降黜有差。

translations.literal: Xiu memorialized impeaching Mingzhu and Guozhu for forming a faction and practicing private interest, listing their crimes in detail, and also citing Folun, Fulata, and Fu for collusion; thereupon Mingzhu and the others were demoted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu impeached Mingzhu and Guozhu for forming a faction and pursuing private gain, listing their crimes in detail, and also cited Folun, Fulata, and Fu for collusion. Mingzhu and the others were then demoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 琇直聲震天下。

translations.literal: Xiu's reputation for integrity shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's reputation for integrity shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 遷太常寺卿，再遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then again to Grand Secretariat Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and then Grand Secretariat Academician.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，复遷吏部侍郎，充經筵講官，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was again transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel, served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became Vice Minister of Personnel, served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium, and was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏劾少詹事高士奇與原任左都御史王鴻緒植黨為奸，給事中何楷、修撰陳元龍、編修王頊齡依附壞法，士奇等並休致回籍。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Junior Mentor Gao Shiqi and former Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Hongxu for forming a clique to do evil; supervising secretaries He Kai, Compiler Chen Yuanlong, and Editor Wang Xuling attached themselves and corrupted the law—Shiqi and the others were all retired and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Junior Mentor Gao Shiqi and former Left Censor-in-Chief Wang Hongxu for forming a corrupt clique, and cited supervising secretaries He Kai, Compiler Chen Yuanlong, and Editor Wang Xuling for abetting them. Shiqi and the others were all retired and sent home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，御史張星法劾山東巡撫錢鎯貪黷，鎯奏辨，因及琇嘗致書囑薦即墨知縣高上達等，卻之，遂挾嫌使星法誣劾，下法司訊。

translations.literal: Before long Censor Zhang Xingfa impeached Shandong Governor Qian Hao for greed and corruption; Hao memorialized in defense and mentioned that Xiu had once written asking him to recommend Jimo Magistrate Gao Shangda and others, which Hao had refused, whereupon he bore a grudge and had Xingfa bring a false impeachment; the case was referred to the judiciary for trial.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Censor Zhang Xingfa impeached Shandong Governor Qian Hao for corruption. Hao defended himself and said Xiu had once written asking him to recommend Jimo Magistrate Gao Shangda and others, which he had refused. Bearing a grudge, Hao had Xingfa bring a false charge, and the case went to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 獄未具，琇疏言：「左都御​​史馬齊於會訊時多方鍛鍊，必欲實以指使誣劾罪。

translations.literal: Before the case was concluded Xiu memorialized, saying: "Left Censor-in-Chief Ma Qi at the joint examination practiced extensive fabrication and was determined to establish the charge of directing a false impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Before the case concluded Xiu wrote: "Left Censor-in-Chief Ma Qi at the joint examination fabricated evidence extensively and was determined to convict me of directing a false impeachment.

sentences.zh: 」詔責琇疑揣。

translations.literal: " An edict rebuked Xiu for suspicion and surmise.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict rebuked Xiu for casting suspicion.

sentences.zh: 尋法司奏琇請託事實，當奪官。

translations.literal: Soon the judiciary reported that the facts of Xiu's solicitation were established and he should be stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the judiciary reported that Xiu's solicitation was proved and ruled he should be stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 上以琇平日鯁直敢言，改降五級調用。

translations.literal: Because Xiu was normally upright and daring in speech, the emperor changed the penalty to demotion by five ranks and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiu was normally upright and outspoken, the emperor commuted the penalty to demotion by five ranks and reassignment.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，吏部推琇通政司參議，上命改令予琇休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Ministry of Personnel recommended Xiu for Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission, but the emperor ordered instead that Xiu be granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the Ministry of Personnel recommended Xiu for Vice Commissioner of the Court of Transmission, but the emperor ordered him retired instead.

sentences.zh: 江寧巡撫洪之傑以吳江縣虧漕項，事涉琇，牒山東追琇赴質。

translations.literal: Jiangning Governor Hong Zhijie, on account of a shortfall in grain transport funds in Wujiang County involving Xiu, sent a dispatch to Shandong summoning Xiu to answer the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangning Governor Hong Zhijie, citing a shortfall in grain transport funds in Wujiang County that involved Xiu, summoned him from Shandong to answer the charge.

sentences.zh: 時佛倫為山東巡撫，因劾琇違例逗留希進用，請奪官逮治；

translations.literal: At the time Folun was Governor of Shandong and impeached Xiu for staying on in violation of regulations in hope of reappointment, asking that his office be revoked and he be arrested for trial;
translations.idiomatic: Folun was then Governor of Shandong and impeached Xiu for lingering in violation of regulations in hope of reappointment, asking that he be stripped of rank and arrested;

sentences.zh: 又劾琇世父郭爾印乃明季御史黃宗昌家奴，琇父郭景昌原名爾標，嘗入賊黨伏法，琇私改父名請誥封，應追奪。

translations.literal: he also impeached Xiu on the ground that his father's elder brother Guo Eryin had been a household slave of the late-Ming censor Huang Zongchang, that Xiu's father Guo Jingchang had originally been named Erbiao and had once joined bandits and suffered execution, and that Xiu had privately changed his father's name to seek ennoblement edicts—all of which should be posthumously revoked.
translations.idiomatic: he also charged that Xiu's father's elder brother Guo Eryin had been a slave of the late-Ming censor Huang Zongchang, that Xiu's father Guo Jingchang had originally been named Erbiao and had joined bandits and been executed, and that Xiu had changed his father's name to obtain ennoblement—all of which should be revoked.

sentences.zh: 部議如所請，逮赴江寧勘治。

translations.literal: The ministries approved as requested, and he was arrested and sent to Jiangning for investigation and trial.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved, and he was arrested and sent to Jiangning for trial.

sentences.zh: 坐侵收運船飯米二千三百餘石，事發彌補，議遣戍，詔寬之。

translations.literal: He was found guilty of unlawfully taking more than twenty-three hundred shi of rice for transport boats' provisions; when the matter came to light he made restitution; banishment was proposed, but an edict granted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He was found guilty of taking more than twenty-three hundred shi of rice meant for transport boats. When the matter came to light he made restitution. Banishment was proposed, but the emperor granted leniency.

sentences.zh: 三十八年，上南巡，琇迎駕德州。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year the emperor made a southern tour, and Xiu met the imperial procession at Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year, on the emperor's southern tour, Xiu met the procession at Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 既還京師，諭大學士阿蘭泰等曰：「原任左都御史郭琇，前為吳江令，居官甚善，百姓感頌至今。

translations.literal: After returning to the capital he instructed Grand Secretary Alantai and others, saying: "Former Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu, once magistrate of Wujiang, governed very well, and the people praise him to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he told Grand Secretary Alantai and others: "Former Left Censor-in-Chief Guo Xiu, once magistrate of Wujiang, governed very well, and the people still praise him.

sentences.zh: 其人有膽量，可授湖廣總督，令馳驛赴任。

translations.literal: The man has courage and may be appointed Governor-General of Huguang; order him to take post by urgent relay.
translations.idiomatic: He has courage. Appoint him Governor-General of Huguang and send him posthaste to take office.

sentences.zh: 」琇上官，疏言：「黃州、武昌二府兵米二萬七千有奇，運給荊州、鄖陽汛地，懸隔千里，輓輸費不貲，請改折色。

translations.literal: " When Xiu assumed office he memorialized, saying: "The two prefectures of Huangzhou and Wuchang supply more than twenty-seven thousand units of military grain to garrison posts at Jingzhou and Xiangyang, separated by a thousand li; transport costs are beyond reckoning—I ask that payment be converted to silver.
translations.idiomatic: " On taking office Xiu wrote: "Huangzhou and Wuchang supply more than twenty-seven thousand units of military grain to garrisons at Jingzhou and Xiangyang a thousand li away. Transport costs are enormous. I ask that payment be converted to silver.

sentences.zh: 江夏等十三州縣有故明籓產，田瘠賦重，數倍民糧，請一律減徵。

translations.literal: Thirteen prefectures and counties including Jiangxia hold former Ming princely estates whose fields are poor yet heavily assessed, several times ordinary people's grain tax—I ask uniform reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen prefectures and counties including Jiangxia hold former Ming princely estates whose fields are poor yet taxed several times the ordinary rate. I ask uniform reduction.

sentences.zh: 江夏、嘉魚、漢陽三縣瀕江地，水齧土陊，有賦無田者三百餘頃，請豁免。

translations.literal: In Jiangxia, Jiayu, and Hanyang, riverside land eroded by water has more than three hundred qing taxed though no fields remain—I ask exemption.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxia, Jiayu, and Hanyang, more than three hundred qing of riverside land eroded by water are still taxed though no fields remain. I ask exemption.

sentences.zh: 」皆允行。

translations.literal: " All were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " All were approved.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，入覲，因奏言：「臣父景昌，即墨縣諸生，有冊可稽。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he came to audience and memorialized, saying: "Your subject's father Jingchang was a licentiate of Jimo County, verifiable in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he came to audience and said: "My father Jingchang was a licentiate of Jimo County, verifiable in the registers.

sentences.zh: 邑匪郭爾標本無妻室，安得有子？

translations.literal: The local bandit Guo Erbiao had no wife—how could he have had a son?
translations.idiomatic: The local bandit Guo Erbiao had no wife. How could he have had a son?

sentences.zh: 不知佛倫何所據，誣臣並及臣父。

translations.literal: I do not know on what Folun relied in slandering your subject and implicating your subject's father.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know what Folun relied on in slandering me and my father.

sentences.zh: 」時佛倫為大學士，上詰之，以舛錯對，命仍予誥軸。

translations.literal: " At the time Folun was Grand Secretary; the emperor questioned him, and he answered with errors; the emperor ordered that the patent of honor still be granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Folun was then Grand Secretary. The emperor questioned him, and his answers were confused. The emperor ordered that Xiu's patent of honor still be granted.

sentences.zh: 琇陛辭，奏請清丈地畝，並言湖南地廣人稀，恐清丈後賦當差減。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience Xiu memorialized asking for a full land survey, and said that Hunan is broad with sparse population, fearing that after survey the assessments would need substantial reduction.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience Xiu asked for a full land survey and said that Hunan is broad and sparsely peopled, so assessments would likely need substantial reduction after survey.

sentences.zh: 上問：「當減幾何？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "How much should be reduced?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "By how much should they be reduced?

sentences.zh: 」琇言：「當減十分之三。

translations.literal: " Xiu said: "They should be reduced by three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiu said: "By three-tenths.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「果益民，雖倍於此，亦不惜也！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "If it truly benefits the people, even double that would not be regretted!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "If it truly benefits the people, I would not regret even double that!

sentences.zh: 」尋條陳三事：一，嚴定築堤處分；

translations.literal: " Soon he set forth three items in detail: first, strict penalties for dike construction;
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he proposed three measures: first, strict penalties for dike construction;

sentences.zh: 一，停造無用糧船；

translations.literal: second, halt building useless grain boats;
translations.idiomatic: second, halt building useless grain boats;

sentences.zh: 一，通融調補苗疆官吏。

translations.literal: third, flexibly transfer and fill Miao frontier posts.
translations.idiomatic: third, flexibly transfer and fill Miao frontier posts.

sentences.zh: 又疏禁徵賦諸弊政。

translations.literal: He also memorialized forbidding abuses in tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to forbid abuses in tax collection.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其實心除弊，並允行。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his sincere heart in removing abuses and approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his sincere effort to remove abuses and approved all.

sentences.zh: 時紅苗就撫，琇陳善後之策，請頒詔敕，令勒石永遵。

translations.literal: At the time the Red Miao had submitted to pacification; Xiu set forth policies for aftermath, asking that an edict be promulgated and inscribed on stone for perpetual observance.
translations.idiomatic: The Red Miao had just submitted. Xiu proposed policies for the aftermath and asked that an edict be promulgated and inscribed on stone for perpetual observance.

sentences.zh: 四十年，以病乞休，上曰：「琇病甚，思一人代之不可得，能如琇者有幾人耶？

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he pleaded illness and asked to retire; the emperor said: "Xiu is very ill; to think of one man to replace him and not find him—how many men are there like Xiu?
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he pleaded illness and asked to retire. The emperor said: "Xiu is very ill. I cannot think of anyone to replace him. How many men are there like Xiu?

sentences.zh: 」給事中馬士芳劾湖廣布政使任風厚久病，巡撫年遐齡徇庇不以聞。

translations.literal: " Supervising Secretary Ma Shifang impeached Huguang Provincial Administration Commissioner Ren Fenghou for long illness, charging that Governor Nian Xialing had shielded him and not reported it.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising Secretary Ma Shifang impeached Huguang Provincial Administration Commissioner Ren Fenghou for long illness, charging that Governor Nian Xialing had shielded him and not reported it.

sentences.zh: 遐齡奏風厚實無病。

translations.literal: Xialing memorialized that Fenghou was in fact not ill.
translations.idiomatic: Xialing reported that Fenghou was not ill.

sentences.zh: 風厚入覲，上見其未衰，因曰：「任風厚若不堪任使，郭琇豈肯徇庇耶？

translations.literal: Fenghou came to audience; the emperor saw he was not enfeebled and therefore said: "If Ren Fenghou were unfit for service, would Guo Xiu have been willing to shield him?
translations.idiomatic: Fenghou came to audience. The emperor saw he was not enfeebled and said: "If Ren Fenghou were unfit for service, would Guo Xiu have shielded him?

sentences.zh: 」未幾，琇以病劇再疏求罷，仍慰留。

translations.literal: " Before long Xiu, his illness severe, again memorialized asking to be dismissed, but was still comforted and retained.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Xiu, gravely ill, again asked to be dismissed, but was comforted and retained.

sentences.zh: 黃梅知縣李錦催科不力，琇委員摘印。

translations.literal: Huangmei Magistrate Li Jin was ineffective in collecting taxes; Xiu sent an officer to remove his seal.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmei Magistrate Li Jin was ineffective in tax collection. Xiu sent an officer to remove his seal.

sentences.zh: 錦得民心，民閉城拒之，乞留錦。

translations.literal: Jin had won the people's hearts; the people closed the city and resisted, begging that Jin be kept.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had won the people's hearts. They closed the city and resisted, begging that he be kept.

sentences.zh: 御史左必蕃劾琇，部議當奪官，上以清丈未畢，緩之。

translations.literal: Censor Zuo Bifan impeached Xiu; the ministries held he should be stripped of office, but because the land survey was not finished the emperor deferred the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zuo Bifan impeached Xiu. The ministries ruled he should be stripped of office, but because the land survey was unfinished the emperor deferred action.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，鎮筸諸生李定等叩閽奏紅苗殺掠，總督、巡撫匿不以聞；

translations.literal: In the forty-first year students Li Ding and others of Zhenqian petitioned at the gate, reporting Red Miao killings and plunder, which the governor-general and governor had concealed and not reported;
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year students Li Ding and others of Zhenqian petitioned at the gate, reporting Red Miao killings and plunder that the governor-general and governor had concealed;

sentences.zh: 而給事中宋駿業亦劾琇向騖虛聲，近益衰廢，持祿養癰。

translations.literal: and Supervising Secretary Song Junye also impeached Xiu for formerly chasing empty reputation, lately growing ever more decayed and negligent, holding his stipend while nursing his malady.
translations.idiomatic: and Supervising Secretary Song Junye also impeached Xiu for chasing empty reputation, lately growing negligent, and holding his stipend while nursing his malady.

sentences.zh: 乃命侍郎傅繼祖、甘國樞，浙江巡撫趙申喬往按。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Vice Ministers Fu Jizu and Gan Guoshu and Zhejiang Governor Zhao Shenqiao to investigate on site.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Vice Ministers Fu Jizu and Gan Guoshu and Zhejiang Governor Zhao Shenqiao to investigate.

sentences.zh: 會琇報清丈畢，乞罷任。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiu reported the land survey finished and asked to be relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Xiu reported the land survey finished and asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 上責其清丈稽延，與前奏不合，行不顧言；

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for delay in the survey, inconsistency with his earlier memorial, and conduct that did not match his words;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for delaying the survey, contradicting his earlier memorial, and acting against his own words;

sentences.zh: 並及匿報紅苗殺掠與黃梅拒命事。

translations.literal: and also cited concealing reports of Red Miao killings and plunder and the Huangmei defiance of orders.
translations.idiomatic: and also cited concealing Red Miao raids and the Huangmei defiance of orders.

sentences.zh: 琇自陳老病失察，請治罪。

translations.literal: Xiu confessed that old age and illness had caused neglect and asked to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu confessed that age and illness had caused neglect and asked to be punished.

sentences.zh: 初紅苗犯鎮筸，游擊沈長祿往剿，至大梅山，守備許邦垣、千總孫清俱陷賊，長祿私贖之歸，諱不報；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Red Miao attacked Zhenqian, Guerrilla Commander Shen Changlu went to suppress them; at Damei Mountain Garrison Commander Xu Bangyuan and Battalion Commander Sun Qing both fell into the rebels' hands, and Changlu privately ransomed them back but concealed the matter and did not report it;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Red Miao attacked Zhenqian, Guerrilla Commander Shen Changlu went to suppress them. At Damei Mountain Garrison Commander Xu Bangyuan and Battalion Commander Sun Qing both fell to the rebels. Changlu privately ransomed them back but concealed the matter;

sentences.zh: 而副將硃紱報苗已就撫，琇據以入告。

translations.literal: yet Vice Commander Zhu Hong reported the Miao had submitted to pacification, and Xiu reported this to the throne on that basis.
translations.idiomatic: yet Vice Commander Zhu Hong reported the Miao had submitted, and Xiu reported this to the throne on that basis.

sentences.zh: 繼祖等勘得狀，琇與提督林本植並奪官。

translations.literal: Jizu and the others verified the facts on investigation, and both Xiu and Provincial Commander Lin Benzhi were stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu and the others verified the facts, and both Xiu and Provincial Commander Lin Benzhi were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 尋祀鄉賢，並祀吳江名宦。

translations.literal: Soon he was enshrined among local worthies and also among the famous officials of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was enshrined among local worthies and also among the distinguished officials of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 論曰：郝浴、楊素蘊秉剛正之性，抗論強籓，曲突徙薪，防禍未形，甘竄逐而不悔。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Hao Yu and Yang Suyun possessed upright and stern natures; they argued against powerful frontier lords, removed the fuel before the fire spread, guarded against calamity before it took form, and accepted exile without regret.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Hao Yu and Yang Suyun were upright and stern by nature. They spoke against powerful frontier lords, removed the fuel before the fire spread, and checked disaster before it formed. They accepted exile without regret.

sentences.zh: 郭琇抨擊權相，有直臣之風，震霆一鳴，僉壬解體。

translations.literal: Guo Xiu struck at the powerful minister with the bearing of an upright remonstrator; one peal of thunder and the whole faction fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiu struck at the powerful minister with the bearing of a true remonstrator. One peal of thunder, and the whole faction fell apart.

sentences.zh: 蓋由聖祖已悟其奸，而琇遂得行其志。

translations.literal: This was because the Sacred Ancestor had already perceived the minister's treachery, and so Xiu was able to carry out his purpose.
translations.idiomatic: This was because the Sacred Ancestor had already seen through the minister's treachery, and so Xiu was able to carry out his purpose.

sentences.zh: 然以浴之廉，蒙議於身後；

translations.literal: Yet for Yu's integrity he suffered censure after death;
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu's integrity was questioned even after his death;

sentences.zh: 素蘊居官愛民，不終於位；

translations.literal: Suyun in office loved the people but did not end his career in post;
translations.idiomatic: Suyun loved the people in office but did not finish his career in post;

sentences.zh: 琇則​​橫被誣陷，廢置十年，始獲申雪。

translations.literal: Xiu was wantonly slandered and imprisoned, set aside for ten years before his name was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was wantonly slandered, set aside for ten years, and only then cleared.

sentences.zh: 得君如聖祖，猶不克善全，直道難行，不其然哉？

translations.literal: With a ruler like the Sacred Ancestor they still could not be preserved intact—how hard the straight path is to walk; is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Even with a ruler like the Sacred Ancestor they still could not be preserved intact. How hard the straight path is to walk—is it not so?
